text: **A third actor breaks the generated admin frontend build (generator bug; contradicts the catalog).** F72 first built as the catalog says (best-practices/model/token-based-verification-workflow.md "Public entry points need an anonymous actor", agent-docs/model/esm_metamodel/accesspoint.md "Anonymous vs Authenticated Behaviour"): actor `PaymentGateway` (kind SYSTEM, anonymous, no principal) with one access. The model validates, backend and REST are generated (route `/api/webshop/PaymentGateway/<TO>/<op>`), but `./judo.sh build` stops in the frontend module `webshop__admin` at `pnpm run format` (biome): "Declarations inside of a `import` declaration may not have duplicates", e.g. `import type { CsvFile, CsvFile, CsvFileStored, CsvFileStored }` in every dialog of an operation with an input AND an output in the admin module (ExportOrders, InviteAdmin, ChangePrices, ImportProducts and the new one); the template helper `getApiImportsForPage`/`classDataName` returns the type twice. Bisected with `build -f -i` (26 s per try): gone when the actor is removed; present for any third actor (kind HUMAN or SYSTEM, anonymous true or false, with or without an access, renamed so it sorts before Admin). The catalog says the opposite: best-practices/frontend/dual-actor-frontend-architecture.md "The pattern extends to three or more actors ... an anonymous public actor next to authenticated staff actors". kb_search "third actor ... duplicate import" found nothing. Kind: generator bug + catalog contradiction (not a model error). Consequence: R16-4.

**`build` without `-i` fails on every generated frontend file, because the build itself reformats them (answer to review R16-R14, which was wrong).** Tried `./judo.sh generate` and `build` without `-i` as REVIEW-R16 R16-R14 suggested: "There are manual changes in the generated files" listing every file of `src/` in both actors. Reason found: `build -i` leaves `.generated-files` of the frontend module EMPTY (0 bytes) and the build formats the generated code with biome (`pnpm run format`) after writing it, so no later run can match checksums. agent-docs/frontend/README.md "Build fails with checksum mismatch error" Option 3 and README.agent.md name `-i` for "formatting-only changes" but do not say that every build produces them, so `-i` is the normal way here and the checksum protection cannot be switched on later without regenerating `src/` from scratch. No generated file was patched.

**How an actor reaches a static operation (catalog gap, answered by trying).** agent-docs/model/esm_metamodel/operation.md "In TransferObjectType (unmapped)" ends with "*Verify:* how an actor reaches the operation (access or menu item) was not settled in source". Tried: unmapped TO as access target -> validator "Access target have to be mapped". Working: a transfer object mapped to the one `ShopConfig` row (`PaymentGatewayInfo`, no members), a STATIC operation on it, and a DERIVED 0..1 access `webshop::ShopConfig!any()` on the actor; the REST route is `POST /api/webshop/<Actor>/<TO>/<operation>` with the input as the JSON body (same shape as the existing table operations, e.g. `/AdminOrderInfo/exportOrders`). A fault comes back as 422 with `X-Fault`. A void static operation is possible. The access needs the settings row to exist.

**F72 webhook is a technical call with a bearer token of the Admin actor, not an anonymous endpoint (least-bad documented route after R16-1).** The static operation `webshop::PaymentGatewayInfo.receive` hangs on a (hidden, not in any menu) Admin access `gateway`. The provider (or the gateway in front of it) calls it with a token of a technical admin user; the call is protected twice: the token and an HMAC-SHA256 signature of `eventId|orderNumber|status` with the shared secret `WEBSHOP_PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (default `dev-webhook-secret`, set it in the environment). Not verified: a real provider; a truly public endpoint (see R16-1). Idempotency key = the provider's event id, stored on the order (`SalesOrder.paymentEventId`).

**`build -a`, `build -F -KA` update `~/.m2` but NOT `application/.karaf/system`, and `./judo.sh start` runs the `system` copies (catalog gap / wrong).** After `./judo.sh build -F -KA` the app started without my four new custom operation classes: health `/system/health` 503 "Missing SDK operations: webshop.ShopJobs#releaseExpired, ...#receive, ...#payNow, ...#releaseReservations" and calls answered 500 `InternalServerException ... IllegalArgumentException: Not implemented yet` (DefaultDispatcher.callOperation). The jars: `application/.karaf/system/com/example/webshop/webshop-application-app/...jar` 14:30 without the classes, `~/.m2/.../webshop-application-app-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` 14:45 with them. Same for the interceptors bundle (a new interceptor was never called). agent-docs/deployment/local-development.md and the `judo.sh` help say `build -a` is "useful for updating custom operations for running backend"; in this layout only a full `./judo.sh build` (4 min) puts new bundles into `system`; once the running app also stopped by itself during `build -a`. Searched: kb_search "Missing SDK operations health check OperationsCheck" (agent-docs/deployment/README.md names the check, not this cause).

**Scheduled job: the platform has no scheduler and the operation name for `Dispatcher.callOperation` is not documented.** Read: agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.md "Scheduled Work" (no scheduler, no ACTOR, call a modeled operation through the Dispatcher), model-blueprints/osgi-scheduled-background-jobs/backend.md, best-practices/backend/quartz-scheduled-job.md (Quartz and `UserTransaction` need extra dependencies: the app module's pom is generated, so not possible without a generated-file edit). Built the documented minimum: an OSGi component with its own `ScheduledExecutorService` (`ReservationJob`, every 60 s, `WEBSHOP_RESERVATION_JOB_SECONDS`) that calls a modeled STATIC operation on an unmapped TO (`webshop::ShopJobs.releaseExpired`, no actor, so no REST route) through `dispatcher.callOperation("webshop.ShopJobs#releaseExpired", new HashMap<>())`. The name format `<asm package>.<class>#<operation>` is nowhere in the catalog (interceptors.md shows only the `...services...#_createInstance...` forms); found it in `application/model/target/generated-resources/model/webshop-asm.model`. The job works (releases through the same service as the admin button, covered by the integration tests; the browser test uses the button).

**No catalog recipe for "provider switched by configuration" with a value an admin can change.** best-practices/backend/external-api-adapter-pattern.md and model-blueprints/external-api-adapter-provider-pattern/backend.md describe interface + adapter per provider + factory that reads a stored "platform" value and credentials; agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.md "Configuration Mapper for Custom Parameters" is an OSGi configuration route that needs `ConfigurationAdmin` and a configset in the generated Karaf module. Chosen: the provider is an enum on the existing settings row (`ShopConfig.paymentProvider`: STUB_SUCCEED, STUB_FAIL, STUB_TIMEOUT, HTTP), editable in "Shop settings", so the browser test switches it; deployment values (URL, key, webhook secret) are system properties or environment variables (`Config.get`). Note: the kb_get of `external-api-adapter-pattern.md` (section "Practice", and the file name) returns "not found" / only a keyword line; the useful text was in `model-blueprints/external-api-adapter-provider-pattern/backend.md`.

**An injectable clock that a running application can move is not in the catalog.** best-practices/backend/injectable-business-clock.md: a holder read once at class load from a property or environment variable (our `BusinessClock`, GAPS R10). That cannot be changed from a browser test. F73 solved with parameters instead of a global: `ReservationService.releaseExpired(LocalDateTime now)` takes the moment (the integration tests pass any date, nothing sleeps) and the admin button "Release expired reservations" has an input "Minutes" that moves the clock forward for that one run (the browser test uses 16). The scheduled job passes `BusinessClock.now()`.

**The generated admin UI never sends `__version`, so optimistic locking does not protect UI edits (catalog says clients echo it).** agent-docs/backend/platform-behavior-reference.md "Optimistic Locking and `__version`": "Clients must echo `__version`"; omitting it disables the check. Found by the browser test: two admins open the same product, one saves stock 11, the other saves a new price: stock went 11 -> 7 silently (audit log rows, DB). Reason in the generated code: `src/services/data-api/common/utils.ts` `applyStoredMembers` copies `__version` only `if (typeof instance.__version === 'string')`, the server sends a number, so it is dropped at load. REST clients that send `__version` are refused with a plain 500 "Outdated instance to update" (no text). Fix without touching generated files: an interceptor on the built-in product update (`ProductConflictInterceptor`, agent-docs/backend/interceptors.md "Throwing a Business Error from an Interceptor") that takes the version from the body or, when none is sent, from the signed identifier of the instance (`update.getInstance().get("__version")`: the signed identifier carries the version of the moment the row was loaded) and refuses with 422 `CONFLICT` and a readable message. Not in the catalog: that the instance payload carries the version of the signed identifier.

**kb problems this round.** `kb_get` returns only a keyword blurb for many "root" sections (`best-practices/backend/external-api-adapter-pattern.md`, `best-practices/model/initializer-operation.md`, `model-blueprints/reservation-booking-entity/BLUEPRINT.md`, `best-practices/backend/correlation-based-event-chaining.md`: the text is in subsections whose names `kb_search` json shows only when a query hits them); `kb_get best-practices/backend/quartz-scheduled-job.md` with section "Practice" -> not found (the real heading is "Practice > Practice notes: scheduler activator, jobs, own transactions"); `kb_get best-practices/backend/external-api-adapter-pattern.md` section "Practice" -> not found. Every search printed "(index refresh still running)" at the start of the round.

**The "extra" i18n fragment cannot override a generated key, so enumeration values show their model names.** Wanted readable labels for the provider enum ("Stub: payment is declined"). `application/frontend-react/generator-overrides/ui-react/actor/public/i18n/application_default_extra.fragment.hbs` (best-practices/frontend/i18n-generator-override-extra-fragment.md) puts the line at the top of `application_default.json`, the generated `enumerations.PaymentProvider.STUB_FAIL` comes later in the same object and wins (last duplicate key). Reverted; the tests use the model names, as for `Unit` (PIECE). An enumeration member has no label in the model (CLI schema: name, documentation, ordinal).

**F72 catalog path does not fit.** FUNCTIONS.md names best-practices/backend/correlation-based-event-chaining.md for the webhook; it is about events chained inside one request (ThreadLocal correlation id), not about processing a duplicate delivery of an external event. Searched "idempotency key duplicate webhook event id" (kb_search json, doc and agents lanes): no page. Built from first principles and tested (integration tests and Playwright: the same event id twice = one transition, one history row; another event for a paid order changes nothing; bad signature 422 INVALID_SIGNATURE; unknown order 422).

**Schema migration and the startup message.** Positive: the migration of this round used the catalog route that now exists (agent-docs/deployment/schema-evolution.md "When No Manual Step Is Needed": `schema_dir=application ./judo.sh schema-upgrade`, additive columns and a new table, 308 orders kept, backup `.scratch/backup-before-r16-9a.sql`); GAPS R12-1 is answered. Unchanged since R1 and not caused by this round: every start logs ERROR `LiquibaseModelDataSourcePrehook ... Could not find compatible schema model` (`NoClassDefFoundError ... EolExecutionContext` in the rdbms osgi bundle) and `/system/health` stays 503 "Missing platform components: InitScriptsCompleted, PersistenceReady" while the application works (reads, writes, custom operations). Not in the catalog (agent-docs/deployment/schema-evolution.md "Troubleshooting" names only "RDBMS model changes which have not been applied").

**No recipe for a partial update with a version.** agent-docs/backend/data-access-guide.md "Pattern 4: Partial Updates" says "set just those fields on an entity that was not loaded in full" but not how to build such an entity with its identifier and version in custom code. Used the generated builder: `ProductBuilder.from(Map.of("__identifier", ..., "__entityType", ..., "__version", ..., "stock", n, "soldUnits", m)).build()` (found by reading the generated `Product.from`); the mask only shapes the read-back (as the doc says), the version check applies because `__version` is in the payload. Covered by integration tests (two transactions that read the same version).

**Earlier specs and the shared dev database (test hygiene; found by the regression run of this round).** Re-ran the older specs against the new build: level 8 (6 tests, checkout, stock, refunds, gift cards, points) and overhaul passed; level 3, 4 and 5 fail in 10 of 24 tests (14 pass) mostly at the step "find the product by name": the admin Products table shows 10 rows per page in database order and the shop home loads the first cards by name, and there are now about 150 products (77 from the seller tests of level 8, 25 from this round), so `adminReadStock` (helpers-customer.ts:167, no filter, no paging), `addFromCard(page, 'Trail mix')` and `getByRole('gridcell', { name: 'Wool socks' })` do not find their row. The `level4` "menu order" test also expects the flat menu of before round 15. Level 7 failed at random steps in two runs after a long session (F58, F59, F61 at different steps; overhaul failed with a screenshot timeout in the same run) and passed 7 of 7 and overhaul 2 of 2 when run alone afterwards. One cause was caught in a screenshot of a failing level9a run: the checkout dialog starts with the focus in "Loyalty points to spend" and digits of the typed address ("Lake Road 9, 5003") landed in that field (it showed 95,003), so the checkout was refused and the helper returned no order number. Level 8 clears the field (resetPoints), level 7 and the first version of level9a did not; level9a now does. Intermittent, so not proven for the level 7 failures (the checkout takes 0.5-2 s in the log; no old build to compare). Not fixed here (no test changes outside level 9a). The level9a spec creates its own products and cannot delete them (a product with orders is deactivated by the delete operation, F29): they stay in the lists. Suggested for the next round: filter by name in the old helpers, give tests a prefix and a cleanup (REVIEW-R16 R16-R21). ## Round 16U (custom UI)

**`kb_get` returns only the intent line of a blueprint or best practice (again R16-10).** For `model-blueprints/cards-container-configuration-hook/BLUEPRINT.md`, `best-practices/frontend/custom-visual-element-override.md` and the other blueprints of this round, `kb_get path` printed one paragraph and "(+9 more sections)"; the sections need `section` with the exact `headingPath`, and a section search returned condensed hits. I read the whole files from `~/Projects/judo-blueprint/catalog/...` on disk instead (that is not possible for a project that has only the kb). Wish: `kb_get` without `section` returns the whole short file.

**A cards container for a relation inside a view cannot be fed by the generated page ("fetch is not a function").** Setting `representationComponent=card` on a to-many relation of a view (order lines, returns, reviews, gift cards, ...) generates a cards container that calls `actions.<relation>RefreshAction`; the generated view page never provides it (the table variant gets it from the lazy table, which fetches by itself). Result: no rows, six console errors per page. The catalog blueprint `cards-container-configuration-hook` and `reservation-booking-entity/frontend.md` ("Cards instead of tables") show cards for relations without this caveat. Route taken: the relation element is a custom implementation element (`best-practices/frontend/custom-visual-element-override`), `representationComponent` stays `table`, and a component reads the rows through the generated service of the view (`list<Relation>`) and renders the shared card (`components/ui/RelationCards.tsx`). Cards containers are used for the screens that are access tables (orders, returns, quotes, ...), where they work.

**The proxy of a relation custom element gets no refresh counter.** `TableProxyProps` (custom/interfaces.ts) has `ownerData`, `isOwnerLoading`, `actions`, `editMode`, but no `refreshCounter`, so a custom list does not know when the page refreshed after an operation (invite, remove). The cards reload when `ownerData` changes identity, and after their own delete/remove action. The generated table gets the counter.

**The generated cards container shows no table operations, no loading state and no empty state.** Create, export (static operation `exportOrders`), the "no results" text and the progress bar of the table are missing; a first conversion lost the "Create" button of the seller's product list and the "Export CSV" button of the orders (found by the level 6a spec). Route: the `ActionbarElement` of the hook renders them (`ListBars.tsx`: create when `actions.openCreateFormAction` exists, extras for table operations such as `exportOrdersAction`, a `LinearProgress`, and an empty state shown by CSS `:has()` when no card follows). The extension-points doc lists `ActionbarElement` but not that it is the only place for these.

**Blueprint sketch uses the old MUI grid API.** `cards-container-configuration-hook/frontend.md` shows `<Grid item xs={12} md={6} lg={4}>`; the generated project (MUI 7) needs `<Grid size={{ ... }}>`, as `agent-docs/frontend/extension-points.md` says. A copy of the blueprint code does not compile.

**The horizontal top bar is a fixed 12-column grid; five menu groups, search, two switches, cart, bell and the profile do not fit.** `HeaderContent` gives the nav `8 - spaceRequired` columns and the right side `2 + spaceRequired`, there is exactly one extra-component slot (`ui-hooks.md` says so), and the scroll arrows of `ScrollableMenu` reserve 2 x 60px. At 1440px the groups were cut ("MY ACCOU>", "COMPAN") and the profile wrapped to a second row. Fixed without touching generated files: `spaceRequired: 2`, global CSS from the extra component (no wrap, the arrows' padding removed, the profile name cut to 96px, smaller switch buttons, the search collapses to an icon until it has focus). At 1280px the last group ("Sell") is behind the scroll arrow. The catalog has no advice on the width of the horizontal menu.

**A detail view cannot be replaced as a whole; every field is its own custom element.** `custom-post-detail-views` says "the view must be a visual element that the UI model declares as a custom implementation". To get one summary layout, all fields of the view are marked `customImplementation=true` (93 elements through the CLI), the title field's element renders the whole layout, the others render `null`, and CSS hides the empty grid cells (`.MuiGrid-root:empty`). Works, but each new field of the transfer object needs a model flag and a registration; a "custom implementation view" option on the page container would be the right shape.

**Data volume of the shared dev database (continues R16-15).** 148 products, 380+ orders and 100+ companies: generated tables show 10-50 rows per page, so specs that find a row by name never saw it. `seekCell` (pages forward) and the card lists' default sort (newest first) fix the old specs. Test products still cannot be deleted when they have orders (F29).

**Not in the model: a review moderation queue and a separate low-stock transfer object.** The round prompt names the review moderation queue as an example of an admin screen. Reviews are written and shown on the product only. The admin screens converted are the dashboard (KPI tiles), the order work queue ("Orders (30 days)", "All orders"), the return-request queue and the quotes. Low stock shares the `ProductInfo` table with the product CRUD, so its card layout would change both; it is a tile of the dashboard.

**Older specs expected markup that earlier rounds had already changed.** The drawer spec expected the side drawer of round 8 (the top bar of round 15 has Products and Cart and drop-downs), the menu-order test expected a flat menu, the F51 branding test clicked group entries as top-level buttons, F40's Hungarian label for the cart needed a non-exact name (the nav items carry a dot icon). Updated, not worked around: `drawer.spec.ts`, `level4.spec.ts` (menu order), `level5.spec.ts`, `level6b.spec.ts`. The shared selectors for rows that are cards or table rows (`cell`, `dataRows`, `emptyList`, `seekCell`, `sortOrdered`) are in `tests/helpers-customer.ts`.

**A full build is still needed for every frontend change that the Playwright suites see.** `./judo.sh build -f -i` regenerates the frontend files but the served application (Karaf) only changes after the full `./judo.sh build -i` and a restart (about 9 minutes with the restart); frontend work was done against the Vite dev server (`VITE_API_DEFAULT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8181 npx vite`) with `playwright.dev.config.ts`. Related to R16-5.

**Profile addresses stay a generated table.** The profile is an editing form with create/update/delete of addresses in the owner's draft; the cards route (R16U-2) would have to re-implement it. The first conversion dropped "Create" there; reverted, `CustomerAccountInfo.addresses` is a table again. The same rows are cards in "My addresses".

**Company pages take 4-9 s with 148 products (a model/performance problem found by the tests; not caused by the UI work).** `POST /Admin/AdminCompanyInfo/~get` and the company list take 4-9 s; `pg_stat_activity` shows one query that computes the derived product fields (`onSale`, `lowStock`, `priceLabel`, ...) for the company-price rows' products, and it grows with the number of products and companies (118 companies, 148 products, 380 orders). Order, product and category lists answer in 0.03-0.5 s. The level 7 specs therefore wait up to 45 s for a response (`slowOpen`, `expect` timeout 15 s in `playwright.local.config.ts`). Suggested for a later round: map the company price's product with only the fields the page shows (a smaller transfer object), or index the join.

**Specs and stock: seeded products are bought by the tests and never restocked.** After a few runs "Wool socks", "Day pack" and others were sold out and unrelated tests failed. `ensureStock(...)` in `tests/helpers-customer.ts` (called in `beforeAll` of the specs that buy seeded products) raises the stock through the admin UI when it is low. The root cause (tests share one database and never clean up) is R16-15 / R16U-8.

**A cards list shows no table operations unless the hook adds them (found by four specs).** Besides R16U-4: row operations of the table (approve and reject of a return request, "Request return", remove of a member) are in the container's `actions` and a card must render them itself; the row operation menus of the tables (three dots) have no counterpart. The shared `makeRowCard` renders `rowActions`, delete and remove; the relation lists pass the page's `<relation>OpenPageAction`, `RowDeleteAction`, `RemoveAction` through `TableProxyProps.actions`.

**The group titles of the top bar are not translated.** "My account", "Company", "Sell" stay English in the Hungarian UI (the entries inside are translated). They are plain strings in `registerShellHooks.ts` (round 15); the menu items customizer has no i18n hook. Noted, not fixed.

**Admin specs and the shared data, and what the reservation job does to exact counts.** The admin Playwright project failed 17 of 35 tests because its specs looked for the 8 seeded products on one page of a table with some 250 products; the seed created a category and a product a second time when the row was on page 2 ("Identifier attribute is not unique", two "Footwear" categories; the duplicate was removed with one SQL delete, it was created by the first run of this round and had no products). Fixed in the specs, not in the data: `seek` pages to the row, the seed checks with `seek`, typing into the generated dialogs is verified and retried (the first field has the focus and takes the first keys; "Commission (%)" of the category dialog is required). Separately, the unpaid orders of earlier tests are cancelled by the reservation job (F73) at any time, which changes the counts of the day (F48) and the stock of seeded products (F23, F49) between two readings; those specs now check the direction of the change, not an exact number. Product price, stock and the name of a seeded product are changed by the shop tests and not restored (`ensureStock` only raises stock).

**Flaky under load: F49 (level6b:85) and F48 (level6b:208), and the Keycloak login timeouts of pw-r16u-q (no product defect).** pw-r16u-final passed 78/78, pw-r16u-final2 76/2. Rerun once each, serially, `--retries=0`: both pass (F49 1.7 min, F48 51 s). Causes: F49 failed on a 10 s `locator.click` timeout (slow page while the Docker VM was loaded; the same spec passes alone); F48 compared the day's order count with a reading taken earlier (expected 97, received 0), which the reservation job (F73) and the data shared with earlier specs can change at any time (see R16U-17). pw-r16u-q had 14 of 15 failures waiting 40 s for `#kc-form-login`; Keycloak (`keycloak-webshop`, port 8280, `/auth`) had 0 restarts, no OOM and answered in 2-10 ms afterwards, other stacks on the same Docker VM were competing for it; the 15 specs pass when re-run (17 passed, 15.3 min). Run Playwright with `-c playwright.local.config.ts --workers=1` and keep other Docker stacks idle during full runs.

**Flaky: F23 (level3-customer:175), final6 failed once (expected stock 57, received 58).** Rerun alone, `--retries=0`: passes (1.8 min). Cause: shared data. The reservation job (F73) cancels old unpaid orders at any time and gives their stock back between two readings, so an exact stock number moves by one. The spec was already changed to check the direction of the change in other places (R16U-17); this one assertion stays exact. Not a product defect. ## Round 17 (Level 9b: F76-F79)

**`kb_get` of a blueprint or best practice returns only the intro line (again, R16U-1).** `kb_get(path)` of `best-practices/backend/scheduled-data-sync-pipeline.md`, `best-practices/model/external-system-staging-entity.md` answered with the Intent paragraph and "(+7 more sections in this file)"; the `kb_search` hits of these files carry only the title as `headingPath` (chunk `:meta`), so no `section` can be copied. The files were read from disk (`/Users/bmiller/Projects/judo-blueprint/catalog/...`). With a `headingPath` from `kb_search` (agent-docs files) `kb_get(path, section)` worked (schema-evolution, build-process, architectural-patterns). There are no `.agent.md` companions for blueprints or best practices, only for agent-docs.

**JUDO CLI: how to create a MIME type, and a binary type with two MIME types.** `judo-cli.agent.md` says `create -t MimeType -n ...` fails (no name) but gives no working form. Found with `create --schema -t MimeType` (route `addMimeType(model, type, subType)`): `create -t MimeType --ns webshop -s type=application -s subType=json`. `BinaryType.mimeTypes` takes ONE value on `create` (`-s mimeTypes=a,b` is rejected) and `--add mimeTypes=...` is rejected too; both print `valid hu.blackbelt...MimeTypeImpl@2f27c354 · ...` (the valid values as object hashes, unreadable) and exit 0, so a script goes on. The failed `create -t BinaryType` left the input member without a data type, and the validation then said "ImportRunInfo_Table::startImport::FormCall have to be presented in container": a misleading message for a missing type (found by `--schema`/`status`). Route: two file members on the input (`csvFile` with the CSV type, `jsonFile` with a JSON type) and a check in the operation that exactly one is given.

**Mail: `JUDO_PLATFORM_MAIL_SMTP_HOST/PORT` in `judo-karaf.env` is not enough to get an `EmailService` (deployment doc incomplete).** `agent-docs/deployment/application-config.md` "6. Email (SMTP)" says: for Mailpit point host and port at `localhost:1025` in `judo-karaf.env`. With host, port, `_AUTH=false` and `JUDO_PLATFORM_LOG_SMTP_SERVER=false` the application started, but the `EmailService` OSGi service did not exist (my `@Reference` was null: "The platform mail service is not available"): `JavaMailSenderActivator` has `configuration-policy=require` and its configuration is created from `judo-platform-config-templates/hu.blackbelt.email.impl.JavaMailSenderActivator.xml`, whose condition is `logSmtpServer || (mailSmtpUser && mailSmtpPassword && mailSmtpHost all set)`. With the log server off, user and password must be set too (any value; `AUTH=false` keeps them unused). Final `judo-karaf.env`: HOST=localhost, PORT=1025, USER=mailpit, PASSWORD=mailpit, AUTH=false, STARTTLS_ENABLE=false, FROM, `LOG_SMTP_SERVER=false`. Read from the jar in `.karaf/system/hu/blackbelt/judo/platform/judo-platform-config-templates`.

**Mail doc: port of the log SMTP server.** The same section says the log SMTP server listens on `logSmtpServerPort`, "which defaults to `1025`"; the shipped template `hu.blackbelt.email.impl.LogSmtpServer.template` says `${logSmtpServerPort ! "10025"}` (and the component XML property is 10025). Read, not run (the log server was off).

**`handlebars-email-template.md` renders twice if the example is copied.** The example compiles the template itself and hands the result to the mail builder as `htmlTemplate`; `platform-behavior-reference.agent.md` "Email Service" says `htmlTemplate`/`plaintTemplate` ARE Handlebars templates applied to `model`, and `subject` is NOT a template. The result of the first rendering is rendered a second time (a value that contains `{{` would be eaten). Used here: the shop renders subject and body itself (to keep the text in the outbox and in the "Sent mails" screen) and passes the text with an empty model. The best practice does not say which of the two is the intended split.
